theme: SpaceX's AI-led beat and merger talk meet Tesla's earnings tonight, while bitcoin's bounce tests Strategy's cushion and AI credit stays tight.

items.title: SpaceX revenue by segment
items.picked: SpaceX reported Q3 last night: revenue of $14.6B, up 161% from a year earlier, beating the ~$12.7B estimate. This chart shows how the business was split before that print.
items.matters: The chart's title calls Starlink 'the business', but in Q3 the Super Intelligence segment brought in $7.56B against $5.25B for Connectivity. The revenue mix is shifting fast toward AI, which changes how SPCX should be valued.
items.know: In the chart (through Jun 30, 2026), trailing-12-month revenue was $13.9B for Connectivity, $5.1B for AI and $4.1B for Space. It does not include Q3 yet. The Q3 release shows quarterly SI revenue alone ($7.56B) already exceeded the chart's whole trailing-year AI figure.

items.title: Starlink subscribers
items.picked: Starlink subscriber growth was a headline in last night's SpaceX results. Consumer subscribers reached 13.6M at the end of Q3, up from 12.0M in Q2, and monthly ARPU rose to $69 from $66.
items.matters: Subscriber growth is what drives Connectivity, SpaceX's most profitable segment ($2.37B of Q3 operating income). ARPU stopping its fall suggests growth isn't coming only from cheaper markets.
items.know: The chart runs through Jun 30, 2026, at 12.0M subscribers, up from 2.3M at the end of 2023 and 6.0M in mid-2025. The Q3 figure of 13.6M from the earnings release isn't in the sheet yet, and the series skips Q3 2025.

items.title: SpaceX vs Tesla market cap
items.picked: On last night's call Musk said a Tesla merger would be a 'good idea' and that both boards have formed special committees to discuss it. Tesla reports Q3 after the close today.
items.matters: In a merger, the exchange ratio would be set by how the two companies are valued against each other, and this chart tracks exactly that.
items.know: As of Oct 16, SpaceX was worth $1.92T and Tesla $1.40T, or 1.37x. The peak was 1.74x on Jun 16, 2026. The data ends before SPCX's roughly 8% after-hours jump on the earnings beat.

items.title: Tesla quarterly capex
items.picked: Tesla reports Q3 after the bell today (call at 5:30 PM ET). Consensus sees about $8.0B of Q3 capex and negative free cash flow, and Tesla guides to more than $25B of capex for 2026.
items.matters: Spending on Cybercab, Optimus, Semi and AI compute is the main reason Tesla's free cash flow has turned negative. Tonight's number will show how fast that spending is climbing.
items.know: Quarterly capex was $5.79B in Q2 2026, more than double the $2.39B a year earlier. Q1 2026 was $2.49B. The chart ends at Q2. Hitting the >$25B full-year guide would take about $17B more across Q3 and Q4.

items.title: Tesla FSD subscriptions
items.picked: FSD adoption is one of the main numbers to watch in Tesla's Q3 report tonight. Tesla's Oct 19 shareholder letter said FSD (Supervised) has nearly 1.5M paid customers.
items.matters: Paid FSD is high-margin software revenue and the user base for robotaxi. It is also one of the milestones in Musk's CEO performance award.
items.know: Active subscriptions rose from 0.95M in Q2 2025 to 1.48M in Q2 2026, up 56% in a year. The latest point is Q2. Tonight's report should give Q3. The count includes upfront purchases and monthly subscriptions, not free trials.

items.title: Texas robotaxi fleets
items.picked: How Cybercab scales beyond Austin is the most-upvoted shareholder question for Tesla's call tonight. NHTSA has given Tesla until Oct 30 to explain how it certified a car with no steering wheel or pedals.
items.matters: This chart compares Tesla's robotaxi fleet with its competitors in the one state where Cybercab runs. It counts vehicles registered with the state, which is harder to spin than company claims.
items.know: As of Oct 11, the Texas DMV registry showed 739 Tesla vehicles (420 Model Y and 319 Cybercabs), against 1,185 for Waymo, 344 for Avride and 63 for Zoox. These are registered vehicles, not cars carrying riders. Tesla said about 311 were active in the 30 days to September.

items.title: MSTR mNAV premium
items.picked: Bitcoin touched $84K this morning, and Samson Mow called Strategy 'massively undervalued' in an interview published today. MSTR rose about 5% on Tuesday.
items.matters: mNAV is the market value of the whole company divided by the value of its bitcoin. Below 1x, the stock is worth less than the coins it holds, which makes issuing new shares to buy more bitcoin dilutive.
items.know: On Oct 16, mNAV was 0.89x, with a $61.8B diluted market cap against $69.1B of bitcoin. It was about 1.0x in late September and early October, and 2.18x in January 2025. This week's rally isn't in the data yet.

items.title: MSTR average purchase price vs BTC
items.picked: On Oct 19 Strategy disclosed 267 more BTC, bringing it to 848,517 BTC at an average cost of $75,446. Saylor said this week Strategy will stay a net buyer but may sell some bitcoin to fund dividends.
items.matters: The gap between the bitcoin price and Strategy's average cost is its cushion. It is what makes the 'sell BTC to pay dividends' question either theoretical or real.
items.know: In the sheet, the average cost was $75,444 on Oct 12 and bitcoin closed at $82,018 on Oct 18. That puts bitcoin about 9% above Strategy's cost basis. At today's ~$84K the cushion is about 11%. The average cost now rises only slightly with each small weekly buy.

items.title: STRC buybacks vs weekly volume
items.picked: On Oct 19 Strategy said it bought back $193.1M of STRC in a single week and raised its preferred buyback authorization from $2B to $3B.
items.matters: Strategy's own repurchases make up a large share of STRC's trading. That supports the price near par, and it is paid for out of the USD Reserve.
items.know: Buybacks were 29.6% of STRC volume in the week of Oct 5, the highest in the chart. The sheet also has the Oct 12 week at 19.6% ($193.1M). The image shows weeks through Oct 5. The total since the week of Jul 20 is $1.84B.

items.title: AI borrower CDS
items.picked: Worries about debt-funded AI spending are back in the news this week, with Oracle and data-center credit spreads near record wides. SpaceX's results last night show $16.4B of quarterly AI capex.
items.matters: Credit default swaps price the risk of a company not paying its debt. They show where bond investors see strain in the AI build-out before stock prices do.
items.know: Oracle's 5-year CDS was 261bp on Oct 9, after a record 265bp on Oct 8. SpaceX was at a record 197bp on Oct 7. Microsoft was 52bp and the investment-grade index 55bp. These levels come from public posts quoting paywalled data, dated Sep 26 to Oct 9, so they are a snapshot, not a time series.
